name: Jairus
role: Synagogue leader whose daughter Jesus raised
whenBasis: Jesus' ministry, from the fifteenth year of Tiberius (Luke 3:1), AD 28–29, to the crucifixion under Pilate, usually dated AD 30 or 33.
summary: A leader of the synagogue, probably at Capernaum, who fell at Jesus' feet and pleaded for his little daughter, who was dying. On the way Jesus stopped for a woman healed of bleeding, and messengers came to say the girl was dead. Jesus told Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe,” put out the mourners, took the girl by the hand and said, “Talitha koum!” She got up and walked; she was twelve years old.
body: Jesus takes only Peter, James and John and the child's parents into the room. He tells them to give her something to eat, and not to tell anyone.

media.caption: The daughter of Jairus (Mark 5:41), James Tissot, 1886–94, Brooklyn Museum.
